title: How to Clean a Pipe or Bong
seoTitle: How to Clean a Pipe or Bong: A Simple Guide | Uforia Dispensary
description: How to clean a glass pipe or bong with isopropyl alcohol and coarse salt, plus how to rinse and dry it, how often to clean and the safety basics to follow.
lede: A clean pipe or bong tastes better, draws more smoothly and is simply nicer to use. Cleaning glass takes just a few household supplies and a little patience, and most of the time is spent waiting.

sections.heading: Why it is worth the effort
sections.html:
Every session leaves a little resin behind. Over time it builds into a dark, sticky film that can dull flavor, restrict airflow and cloud the glass. Bong water turns stale quickly, too, and water left standing for days can grow mold and bacteria.

Buildup is also easier to remove while it is fresh. A piece cleaned regularly takes a few minutes, while one left for months can need several rounds of soaking.

sections.heading: The alcohol and salt method
sections.html:
The most popular approach for glass uses two inexpensive supplies: isopropyl alcohol, ideally 91 percent or stronger, and coarse salt, such as kosher or sea salt. The alcohol dissolves resin, and the salt acts as a gentle scrubber that reaches places a brush cannot.

  1. Empty the piece, tapping out old ash and pouring out any bong water.
  2. Rinse it with warm water to loosen buildup. Avoid boiling water or sudden temperature changes, which can crack glass.
  3. Remove small parts, such as the bowl and downstem, and place them in a zip-top bag or a small container.
  4. Add a generous spoonful of coarse salt, then pour in enough alcohol to cover the dirty areas.
  5. Cover the openings with your hands, cleaning plugs or plastic wrap, and shake or swirl for a few minutes.
  6. Let stubborn spots soak for a while, then shake again. Pipe cleaners or a soft brush can reach narrow passages.
  7. Pour out the alcohol and salt, then rinse thoroughly with warm water until no alcohol smell remains.

sections.heading: Drying and safety
sections.html:
Isopropyl alcohol is flammable. Work in a well-ventilated space, keep it well away from lighters, candles and stovetops, and never mix it with bleach or other household cleaners. Gloves are a good idea if your skin is sensitive.

Once the piece is rinsed, let it dry completely before you use it again. Leftover alcohol is unpleasant and unsafe to inhale, and it is a fire risk the moment a lighter comes near, so give it time, ideally a few hours or overnight, and make sure the glass smells only of clean water.

This method is meant for glass. Silicone, wood and metal pieces need different care, so check what the maker recommends.

sections.heading: How often to clean
sections.html:
A good rule of thumb is to change bong water after every session, or at least once a day, and to give glass a full cleaning about once a week if you use it regularly. Occasional users can clean less often, but it is always easier before resin has time to harden. A quick warm rinse after each use makes the deep clean faster.

Keeping pipe cleaners, brushes and cleaning plugs on hand makes the routine simple. You can browse the accessories on Uforia's live menu, and our safe consumption page has more everyday tips.

takeaways: Isopropyl alcohol and coarse salt lift resin from glass with a little shaking.
Rinse well with warm water and let the piece dry completely before using it.
Work in a ventilated space away from flames, and never mix alcohol with bleach.
Change bong water often and deep-clean about once a week with regular use.
